Hi all. I'm a girl with a slight frame (5'4'' and ~109lbs) who does predominantly long distance running and enjoys body weight exercises + some weighted machines for glutes, abs, and arms. But I'd really love to start adding more weightlifting to my gym routine. I'm pretty clueless on the matter of free weights and honestly don't know where to start - any advice / good videos for proper form are appreciated!

Also, does anyone (other weightlifting women in particular) have advice for overcoming my fear of the male lifters at my gym? Not that I dislike them or anything like that, I just feel so awkward thinking of going over and doing my modest weights while they're all pumping 180 lbs like it's nothing! Is it just a matter of "the more you do it, the less intimidating it is"? Sorry if this is a stupid question!

-EggHead
Newbie Who Wants to Start Weightlifting. Tips?

Start slow and get a feel for it. If a weight is too heavy, there's no shame in going lighter. As far as others go, don't mind them and worry about what YOU'RE doing.

Form-wise, typically, keep a straight back and the rest will follow. I don't have any video links since I'm on my phone. :-(

No one can really recommend a program without knowing what your goals are. If you just want to try a variety of exercises, I'd strongly suggest just asking a PT for general advice or just look up brosplit routines.

Also, does anyone (other weightlifting women in particular) have advice for overcoming my fear of the male lifters at my gym? Not that I dislike them or anything like that, I just feel so awkward thinking of going over and doing my modest weights while they're all pumping 180 lbs like it's nothing!

I'm no woman, but when I was a newbie, I'd just listen to music and be in my own world for a bit. After being around the same group, just start chatting with the regulars.

The first thing you should do is define your goals. What are you hoping to achieve through weightlifting? Are you aiming for aeasthetics or do you want to get strong as fuck? Are there specific parts of your body you want to improve or do you a full body routine?

I'm not a woman, so my advice about feeling intimidated might not work for you. However, I suggest you try talking to those big scary gym bros. Even just do something simple like ask for a spot. I go to a gym with pro body builders and actively competing powerlifters; there are some massive dudes where I lift. It turns out almost all the big guys are really friendly and are happy to help out newbies.

I have two suggestions for you: http://startingstrength.com/ or https://stronglifts.com/5x5/

Pick one. Both of these programs come with apps to help in your progression. They have great reading material and example videos to help with form. Start small, and work your way up. Everyone started somewhere even the meathead squatting 8 plates.
Alan Thrall has good videos on proper form, at least in my opinion. He's basically showing the techniques from Starting Strength.

Firstly, about routine: I recommend StrongLifts 5x5 because it's a dead simple full body workout. You need to study each of the exercises in depth to really do them safely--but they're only a few, and as a consequence of this, you get to really focus on them. Since you're using a free bar, you get good muscle recruitment, and you practice coordination.

Now, as for the intimidation part!

I started with StrongLifts 5x5 at a gym. So, I walked in, picked up an empty bar, did some super awkward squats with it, put it down and left. Next workout, I was putting on the little 2.5lb donuts and nothing else. It felt embarrassing. But now, I lift so much more than that. I can squat 300lbs, more than 6x the weight of an empty bar.

I've talked with many of the other "heavy lifters" at my gym, and honestly? We all are your cheerleaders. When we see somebody come in and start lifting very light weights, not sure of themselves, we all just have one question in our minds: "How many more times am I going to see you?"

About four of every five newcomers, we see twice or thrice and then they're gone forever. But we're all cheeeing for you. Every time you come back in, we're proud of you. And as you start passing milestones, we'll start saying hi.

Remember, the "high score" of weight lifting has nothing at all to do with how much weight you have moved. The "high score" of lifting is, "how many days have you gone without injury?"

Enjoy, don't round out your back, and most of all, have fun! Being strong is awesome. :)
No male lifter will have any negative thoughts at all about you (as a female) lifting modest weight. Don't feel awkward about that at all, it will not register on anyone's radar one bit.

And don't worry about getting to "muscle-y" like a lot of girls do. You won't suddenly wake up looking like Arnold.
